mechanism.summary: Teach the existing typed-loop dataflow to lower statically indexed property reads, including the fused local-receiver GetPropIndex form, through its guarded dense-array operations. A fixed-index result that feeds another property read stays boxed so general table[row][dynamicIndex] chains can execute in the native loop; a numeric result remains scalar. Every miss deoptimizes at the original bytecode instruction.
mechanism.generality: Admission depends only on immutable bytecode shape and the existing typed-loop fixed point. The encoded index is a standard uint32 property index, the fused receiver must be a live local Array, and every nested receiver and dynamic index must pass the existing present dense-element guards. The mechanism never inspects source paths, benchmark names, constructor or variable names, array sizes, key contents, input values, iteration counts, checksums, or results. A non-fused fixed-index read uses the boxed receiver already present on the operand stack. Non-Arrays, typed arrays, holes, indexed descriptors, inherited indexed properties, accessors, Proxies, out-of-range dynamic indices, unsupported writes or calls, direct eval, and any failed entry or mid-loop guard resume the unchanged interpreter at the exact GetPropIndex or later operation.
semantic_risks: reconstructing the exact operand stack when a fused GetPropIndex has no explicit receiver operand while an ordinary GetPropIndex does
preserving uint32 fixed-index semantics, including holes, inherited indexed properties, indexed descriptors, typed arrays, and non-Array receivers by deoptimizing before observable work
keeping fixed-index results boxed only when later dataflow needs an object receiver, without boxing numeric table values that can remain scalar
preserving live array aliasing, dense writes, branches, descending counters, and mid-loop replay ordering in the existing typed-loop executor
leaving precedence and admission of numeric-mutation, numeric, control, and previously compiled typed-loop programs unchanged

profile_evidence.source: macOS sample 2026-07-31 target/performance-profile-60e28ecf/jetstream-stanford-crypto-aes/current.sample; exact promoted 60e28ecf release executable SHA-256 04d1ea96981f83afe8a34ae83b9d98da17a1d1d641f9bcd9a950d74a4645c6d1; generated source-faithful JetStream bundle SHA-256 7afbe130da966d379938ae8160dada27f991bba82cc0d1b85b4df86f1c2ad94f and diagnostic 12-iteration wrapper SHA-256 94daaa6797bd7ac7d8a438919d836096aa1ba6f15f4a091c8a297ce778fcbb16; the process completed with the expected sentinel and empty stderr
profile_evidence.shared_cost: Of 3,643 main-thread samples, 1,673 (45.9%) land exclusively in generic Vm::run_completion while only 10 land in typed-loop entry. The AES constructor chain contains 2,573 samples. A reverted compiler-only trace (SHA-256 d1c33d14537cd0fde116d8d19adb9ded425a88b6802a17ab891f5df481dda0bc) shows that the first key-expansion loop already compiles, while the second loop at bytecode 214..303 is rejected at four fused GetPropIndex operations that produce the fixed table rows for later dynamic dense reads.

profile_evidence.source: macOS sample 2026-07-31 target/performance-profile-60e28ecf/kraken-stanford-crypto-aes/current.sample; the same exact promoted 60e28ecf release executable; generated source-faithful Kraken bundle SHA-256 c5a8c4ac34189f33a6539e61bda420f6e738a7ebd2028a07a72638b19d0ed16a and diagnostic 40-iteration wrapper SHA-256 05176d71a6aada69d4e3114a5f47fd08a19533c24a6758ab1f9bc3538683e6c4; the process completed with the expected sentinel and empty stderr
profile_evidence.shared_cost: The independent AES corpus reproduces the same key-schedule bytecode and rejection boundary. Of 3,382 main-thread samples, 1,524 (45.1%) land exclusively in generic Vm::run_completion, 2,294 enter the constructor chain, and only 8 reach typed-loop entry. This confirms a shared fixed-index nested-table mechanism rather than JetStream harness or data-specific behavior.
